column6: Core Idea "abolitioner" changed to "abolitionist". Also noted (not fixed): Q0 distractor A defines "Historicism" as judging the past by present standards, which is presentism.
Noted (old Explainer, not fixed): "wave of revisionist scholarship" on the Holocaust is an ambiguous label, since "revisionism" also names Holocaust denial.
Noted (old Explainer, not fixed): structural causes are called "necessary" while the same Explainer says most causes are contributing, not necessary.

Bullet 3 belief ("A portrayal in fiction tells us about the people portrayed") was broader than its correction, which covers only stereotyped portrayals; as stated the belief is often true. Narrowed belief to stereotyped portrayals.
Bullet 4 belief ("Official records tell us mainly about the institutions") is largely true and the correction conceded it; not a real misconception. Changed belief to "can tell us only about".
Noted (old Q1 explanation, not fixed): question is about American industrialization but the examples include Lancashire and Bombay.

Explainer drafting duplication "the sea as connector and connector of" reduced to "the sea as connector of". Also noted (not fixed): Explainer gives événement time as "years to decades"; Braudel's short time is usually glossed as days to months/years.
Noted (old Q0, not fixed): "18th-century European sumptuary laws"; such laws were mainly medieval and early modern and were fading by the 18th century.
Noted (old Q0/Explainer, not fixed): "90% silver under Augustus (1st century BCE)" is loose; Augustan denarii are usually put above 95% fine, and his reign ran 27 BCE to 14 CE.
Noted (old Q1 stem, not fixed): "studying 15th-century Europe" with a 1517 boundary.
Noted (old Explainer, not fixed): attribution of "Napalm Girl" to Nick Ut has been publicly disputed since 2025 (World Press Photo suspended the credit); consider hedging.
Noted (old, not fixed): Q0 dates the first historian 1920, Explainer's parallel example says 1930; Q0 explanation says "not new evidence" while the keyed option says "not necessarily".
Noted (old Q4 answer, not fixed): says hostility and exaggeration "disqualify it as direct evidence", in tension with the file's "bias does not disqualify a source".

Garbled stem "can seldom be answered by examining most available source" (likely a bad never->seldom substitution) rewritten as "When it is impractical to examine every available source for a research question"; answer false still correct.
